target_customer: Consumers who want to build healthy habits, paying a subscription for the Health Month game
problem: People struggle to stick with healthy habits; Health Month turned habit tracking into a game with points and peer support, and Budge (Bud.ge) aimed to let friends motivate one another with if you do x I will do y commitments.
business_model: Consumer freemium subscription (about $5 per month or $50 per year to track more than three rules)

founders.name: Buster Benson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2011 calls him the founder of 43Things, later sold to Amazon, and founder of Health Month. A MobiHealthNews search summary calls him co-founder and CEO at the wind down while TechCrunch 2011 has McCabe as CEO; roles conflict.

founders.name: Jen McCabe
founders.background_notes: Founder of Contagion Health, the Y Combinator company that merged with Health Month. A search summary of MobiHealthNews says she left in March to work for a robotics company; the article itself was not readable.

founders.name: Andrey Petrov
founders.background_notes: Listed as a former founder on the YC page; bio mentions open source and p2p systems.

exit.reason: Per a MobiHealthNews search summary, the company wound down, sold Health Month to Digitally Justified Technologies and said it had run out of money; Bud.ge never left beta.

competitors.name: Mindbloom
competitors.what: Gamified life improvement and wellness product

technical_complexity.rationale: Email nudge based habit tracking with a points game was a lightweight web app; the merged team planned an HTML5 mobile version and an unreleased Habit AI product.

defensibility.rationale: Team play and a small paying community gave mild lock in, but rules, points and email prompts are easy to copy and a competing set of habit apps launched in 2011.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought the company; Health Month was sold to a small Canadian firm on wind down.

market_need_then: Health Month had about 45,000 users in August 2011 with 7 to 12 percent paying (company figures in TechCrunch), showing real consumer pull for gamified habit tracking.

branding.domain_note: Budge product used the bud.ge domain hack (per search summaries); not otherwise verified.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful game framing with life points and nudges (product description)

branding.brand_signature: Health Month game with life points

rebrands.why: Merger of the two startups; Contagion Health's Imoveyou.com was shut in the merger

branding.community_and_virality: Health Month had about 45,000 users in 2011 and about 60,000 users at wind down according to search summaries; no merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Health Month had a modest loyal paying community and TechCrunch coverage, but the Habit Labs and Budge names did not gain recognition and no brand driven growth is sourced.

pivots.from: Contagion Health (Imoveyou) and Health Month as separate products
pivots.to: Habit Labs merged company building Budge and Habit AI
pivots.why: Merger of two startups to build a behavior change platform

outcome_analysis: Habit Labs merged two health startups in August 2011 and raised $250K from angels, with Health Month showing paying users, but its new Budge product never left beta. The company later wound down, sold Health Month to a small Canadian buyer and reportedly ran out of money, while a co-founder left, so the timeline fits a small consumer subscription business that did not reach a venture scale second product.
notes: The MobiHealthNews article returned 403, so its details come from search summaries; one search summary dated a related item July 2017 while another implied an earlier wind down, so the exit date is left null. CB Insights lists $770K across 4 rounds and $270K for Contagion Health (single database); Seedtable lists $250K; another outlet reportedly says $275K from FF Angel and Esther Dyson in 2010, unverified, so funding is partial and about $250K of the $770K is not itemized. The YC page lists no website and the company site is gone. I did not find a source explaining the Habit Labs or Budge names. Competitors are as of the August 2011 merger post, 14 months after the batch, because the company was formed then. The stage of the 2011 round is not labeled as seed in the article, so it is other. Roles differ between sources (CEO McCabe in 2011, CEO Benson at wind down).
